sources.title: Sungei Kadut Eco-District to Attract New Industries and Develop New Capabilities
sources.license_summary: No open reuse license was identified. Paraphrase with attribution; do not reuse JTC branding, photographs, diagrams, or masterplan graphics without permission.
sources.collection_method: Direct web retrieval from the official JTC website on 2026-08-08.
sources.coverage: An approximately 18-hectare Agri-Food Innovation Park within a larger eco-district, co-locating research and development, prototyping, and high-tech farming operations; the district model also uses shared facilities and services.
sources.transformation: Design inference: adapt the co-location principle into a compact food-innovation spine that combines demonstration production, test kitchens, maker space, shared utilities, and public-facing exhibition space.
sources.usage: Use as attributed evidence for agri-food innovation clustering and shared district infrastructure, not as proof of an AI platform, local feasibility, or institutional participation.
sources.limitations: The source supports agri-tech co-location rather than a proven AI or public-market model. Singaporean land, finance, regulation, and industrial demand are not directly transferable, and no JTC relationship is implied.

sources.coverage: Adaptive reuse of a former abattoir as a cluster of restaurants, shops, small-scale food-production facilities, an urban yard open to the public, and recurring events and cooking courses.
sources.transformation: Design inference: treat the central courtyard as shared civic infrastructure connecting visible food-making, small businesses, flexible seating, and a programmable common table.

sources.title: Policy Brief — Hub di Quartiere contro lo Spreco Alimentare Cuccagna

sources.license_summary: No open reuse license was identified. Cite and paraphrase; do not reproduce layouts, photographs, the collective mark, or partner identities as endorsements.

sources.coverage: A neighbourhood-hub network that recovers still-edible surplus from retail, wholesale and open markets, and corporate canteens for redistribution through third-sector operators, with public calls, co-design, operating agreements, and flow monitoring.
sources.transformation: Design inference: reserve a controlled back-of-house node for logged surplus intake, inspection, cold storage, and approved redistribution, separated from public dining and commercial-kitchen flows.
sources.usage: Use as attributed evidence for neighbourhood-scale surplus logistics and multi-actor operating governance, not for nutrition outcomes or a commercial business case.
sources.limitations: This is a food-aid and surplus-recovery model. Local food-safety, liability, cold-chain, beneficiary, and third-sector arrangements require independent design, and no partnership is implied.
